messages:
observability-bot: Alert: Kibana search latency exceeded 10s for index pattern logs-*-* (us-west, eu-west) — triggered 2x during GPU pool scale-up. https://kibana.example/alerts/12345 :rotating_light:

kai: saw this at 03:12 UTC when we added 6 GPU nodes, logs spike looked correlated with model load events.

maria: which trace id are we hunting? paste the id and I'll run a narrow query.

kai: trace.id=abcd-1234-ef56-7890

kai: attempted cross-region loki lookup: 
```
{app="inference", env="prod"} |= "trace_id=abcd-1234-ef56-7890"
| json
| trace_id="abcd-1234-ef56-7890"
```
results: empty in eu-west, timed out in us-west (search timed out after 10s).

ashley: can someone check ES cluster health? sounds like shard activity or disk watermark.

josh: quick check: `curl -s http://es-cluster:9200/_cat/health?v` -> yellow, `curl -s http://es-cluster:9200/_cat/shards | grep us-west` shows multiple UNASSIGNED/INITIALIZING replicas. disk: us-west-log-1 at 95%

ashley: likely cause: hot index for logs-prod-us-west grew past rollover (hot segment merges + GC) during scale-up. big merges -> slow searches.

maria: short term mitigation: scope Kibana query to last 6h and to region:us-west, bump search timeout to 30s for this query. also add `trace.id:"abcd-1234-ef56-7890"` in KQL rather than full-text.

josh: longer term: options: increase replica allocation temporarily, lower refresh_interval for hot indices, or reindex with more shards. also consider dropping heavy field `raw_trace_payload` from logging or move to S3.

ashley: created INF-2345 in Jira (logs: sharded index timeouts during GPU scale events), assigned to eng-sre, priority P1. link: https://jira.example/browse/INF-2345

kai: I'll run a targeted loki query limited to 1h window and post tail results; will also run `/_cat/indices?h=index,pri,rep,docs.count,store.size` to show size.

observability-bot: Policy note: hot indices rollover at 50GB or 24h. Current logs-prod-us-west-2026.03.17 is 72GB (over threshold) — auto-rollover skipped due to pending merges.

deploy-bot: deploy summary: scale-up completed (6 new GPU nodes) at 03:12 UTC, 03:15 health checks passed. correlate with alert spike at 03:12-03:20.

maria: actionable: 1) temporarily increase Kibana/Grafana search timeout to 30s for alert window; 2) add alert suppression while we fix replicas; 3) add correlation-id header in model-load logs to avoid free-text searches.

josh: alert tuning suggestion: only fire SearchLatency alert when avg_latency>10s AND failed_searches>0 for 3/5m windows. reduces noise during transient merges.

ashley: infra task: add 2TB ephemeral to us-west-log-1 to relieve disk watermark, trigger replica recovery. doing now.

kai: ack. muting noisy alert for 30m while we triage :thumbsup:

maria: once replicas recover, re-run the trace lookup and confirm we find the trace in eu-west as well. post results here.

ashley: created followup doc in confluence: "logs: shard sizing & retention playbook" — https://confluence.example/display/INF/log-shard-playbook

josh: note for runbook: consider reducing indexing of `raw_trace_payload` to cutoff >10kb, move payloads to object store with link in doc.

kai: posting loki tail output (snip):
```
2026-03-17T03:12:05Z inference[loader]: model=a13 load start trace_id=abcd-1234-ef56-7890 payload_size=85kb
2026-03-17T03:12:07Z inference[loader]: model=a13 kvcache warmup trace_id=abcd-1234-ef56-7890 time_ms=340
```

maria: good, trace shows in us-west. eu-west missing likely due to delayed replication.

observability-bot: Alert suppressed by kai until 1769549801 (30m).

ashley: leaving action items on INF-2345: increase ephemeral on us-west-log-1, re-run replica allocation, reindex hot index with updated shard count, implement payload archival.

kai: will update thread when replicas green. thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
